title: How much oil does each family get?
description: {{NAME_3}} and two neighbours share five litres of oil every week, and the video finds one family's oil in a week and in four weeks by dividing first and then multiplying, the same way as the example in the book. It ends by checking that three families get the five litres back.
teaching_notes: One idea: sharing five litres among three families is five divided by three, and four weeks is four times that share. Watch for students who write three over five instead of five over three.

source: {{NAME_3}} and two of the neighbours buy 5 litres of oil every week and share it equally among the 3 families. How much oil does each family get in a week? How much oil will one family get in 4 weeks?
video_script.why: The child has multiplied a whole number by a fraction and now first shares a whole number equally, then multiplies the share for more weeks.
video_script.substitution: Five litres shared among three families is five thirds of a litre each, and four weeks is four times that share.
video_script.anchor: Five litres of oil are shared equally among three families: how much does one family get in a week and in four weeks?
video_script.payoff_line: Each family gets five thirds of a litre in a week and twenty thirds in four weeks

final_answer.value: 5/3 litres (1 2/3) in a week and 20/3 litres (6 2/3) in 4 weeks
final_answer.spoken: five thirds of a litre in a week and twenty thirds of a litre in four weeks

video_script.fraction_reading: five thirds, fifteen thirds, twenty thirds

names.{{NAME_3}}: buys 5 litres of oil a week and shares it with two neighbours

maths_rules: oil for one family in a week = 5 ÷ 3 = 5/3 litres = 1 2/3 litres
oil for one family in 4 weeks = 4 × 5/3 = 20/3 litres = 6 2/3 litres
check: 4 weeks × 5 litres = 20 litres for the three families
video_script.design: One idea: share the whole first, then multiply the share for more weeks. Five bars of oil shared among three families are the anchor and stay all video; the working band builds in the idea part.

beats.on_screen: small title card From your book; 5 litres of oil drawn as 5 bars; three families waiting to share; a question mark for one week and one for four weeks

marks.scene: the small title card From your book appears
marks.buy: the five litres of oil and the three families appear
marks.ask: the question marks for one week and for four weeks appear

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about {{NAME_3}}.
<bookmark mark='buy'/>{{NAME_3}} and two neighbours buy five litres of oil every week. They share it equally among the three families.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How much oil does each family get in a week? And how much does one family get in four weeks?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: five bars for the 5 litres of oil of one week, a bracket for three families, and the same picture repeated for four weeks

marks.oil: five bars for the five litres of oil appear
marks.share: a bracket marks three families sharing the bars equally
marks.weeks: the same picture repeats for each of four weeks

narration: <bookmark mark='oil'/>Picture the five litres of oil as five equal bars, one bar for each litre.
<bookmark mark='share'/>Three families share the oil equally.
<bookmark mark='weeks'/>The same sharing happens again in each of the four weeks.

beats.on_screen: Given: oil bought each week = 5 litres; shared equally among 3 families

marks.given: the given lines are written in the working band

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, five litres of oil are bought every week.
The oil is shared equally among three families.

beats.on_screen: To find: oil for one family in 1 week and in 4 weeks

marks.find: the find line is written under the given lines

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the oil one family gets in a week and in four weeks.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: oil for one family in 1 week = 5 litres ÷ 3 = 5/3 litres

marks.one: the line for one week is written

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Step one, find the oil one family gets in a week.
<bookmark mark='div'/>The oil is shared equally among three families, so divide five litres by three.
Five divided by three is five thirds of a litre.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: oil for one family in 4 weeks = 4 × 5/3 litres = (4 × 5) pieces of size 1/3

marks.four: the line for four weeks is written

narration: <bookmark mark='four'/>Step two, find the oil one family gets in four weeks.
Four weeks is four times one week.
<bookmark mark='mult'/>Multiply four by five thirds, the same way as the example in your book.
<bookmark mark='count'/>Four times five is twenty, and each piece is one third.

beats.on_screen: Step 3 (check): 3 × 5/3 = 15/3 = 5 litres; 4 weeks × 5 litres = 20 litres for the 3 families
narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step three, check by putting one family's oil back in the question.
Three families with five thirds of a litre each make fifteen thirds, which is five litres.
<bookmark mark='twenty'/>In four weeks the oil bought is twenty litres, shared by the same three families.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 1 week: 5/3 litres = 1 2/3 litres; 4 weeks: 4 × 5/3 = 20/3 litres = 6 2/3 litres

marks.week: 5/3 litres = 1 2/3 litres is written and boxed
marks.four: 20/3 litres = 6 2/3 litres is written and boxed
marks.pay: both answers stay on the board

narration: <bookmark mark='week'/>Five thirds of a litre is one and two thirds litres.
<bookmark mark='four'/>Four weeks give twenty thirds, or six and two thirds litres.
<bookmark mark='pay'/>Each family gets five thirds of a litre in a week and twenty thirds in four weeks.
